Beep.
A news segment from Beslan in the year 2050 starts playing.
Ladies and gentlemen, we are now standing outside Beslan High School No.1, where the terrorist attack took place.
It has been two days since the tragic event, and as you can see, the school remains sealed off, with nearly all nearby shops still closed.
The camera follows the reporter's gesture, sweeping across the surroundings. The street is desolate, and the once-bustling storefronts are shut tight like wilted flower buds.
Suddenly, the camera zooms in on a single shop that still has its lights on.
We've noticed that a pastry shop is still open. Let's take a closer look.
The shaky camera stops in front of the bakery. A face—nervous and uneasy—appears in front of the lens.
...Who are you?
Hello, I'm a reporter with Central Television of the Neo-Soviet Union, here to follow up on the recent terrorist attack from two days ago.
Would you be willing to speak with us?
Um...
I see most of the shops near the school are closed. Is that because of the attack?
Yeah. After something that big, who wouldn't be scared?
Then why have you chosen to stay open?
...Sigh.
The shopkeeper's gaze drifts away from the reporter, turning toward the shuttered school in the distance.
On the morning of the attack, a little girl in a Beslan High School uniform came in and ordered a cake.
Said she'd pick it up after school, paid for it in full.
She never came back?
No.
I'm still waiting for her to pick it up. I'm hoping… she survived the attack.
Would you mind showing us the cake? Maybe if she—or someone in her family—sees it on the news, they'll come by to collect it.
The shopkeeper gestures toward the refrigerator behind her.
The camera pans over to the clear glass door. Inside the empty, silent case sits a single, lonesome birthday cake.
On the top, two little figures are drawn holding hands, walking through a garden of blooming daisies. Written on a small chocolate plaque below—
Happy Birthday, Mama! Love, Sana.
